boundaries: These semantics describe how already-approved product policies would have to be expressed by a future executor.
No relation is promoted from TO_CONFIRM and no destructive action is authorized.
A row can be operationally specified without being legally/privacy approved for execution.
Schema changes needed to express DETACH/ANONYMIZE remain implementation work, not implicit authorization.

policyDetermined.currentSchemaConstraint: user_id is NOT NULL and NO ACTION, so deleting the user before retained session rows expire is currently blocked.
policyDetermined.implementationConsequence: Future executor must stage account erasure or redesign the session evidence representation; direct root deletion first is invalid.

policyDetermined.currentSchemaConstraint: author_id is NOT NULL and FK-bound; anonymisation requires an explicit schema-supported de-identification mechanism rather than leaving the deleted user id.
policyDetermined.implementationConsequence: Executor can implement DELETE immediately; the exceptional anonymisation path requires schema support and de-identification tests.

policyDetermined.currentSchemaConstraint: author_id is NOT NULL and FK-bound; anonymisation requires explicit schema support and media/reference scrubbing.
policyDetermined.implementationConsequence: Executor can implement DELETE immediately; the exceptional anonymisation path requires schema and media-erasure support.

policyDetermined.currentSchemaConstraint: dog_id is NOT NULL and NO ACTION, so current schema cannot retain device metadata while deleting the dog.
policyDetermined.implementationConsequence: Future implementation needs nullable/detached device ownership or a separate retained security-metadata representation before destructive dog erasure.

policyDetermined.currentSchemaConstraint: product and research rows share one physical table.
policyDetermined.implementationConsequence: Future executor must branch by administration_mode before deleting assessment parents.

policyDetermined.currentSchemaConstraint: database CASCADE is mechanical and will fire if the assessment parent is deleted.
policyDetermined.implementationConsequence: Parent assessment authority must be resolved before deletion; no independent child decision is needed.

authorityDecisionsRemaining.why: Respondent account deletion can affect an assessment attached to another guardian's dog. Deleting the whole assessment may erase another subject's product history; retaining the user id defeats erasure.
authorityDecisionsRemaining.privacyFirstRecommendation: For non-research assessments whose dog remains active, DETACH respondent_user_id (nullable today) and retain respondent_role + non-identifying provenance; if the dog is also erased, delete the assessment. Research rows remain under research governance.

authorityDecisionsRemaining.why: Runtime access authority is membership-scoped; created_by is provenance, so creator erasure does not technically require deleting the multi-party community.
authorityDecisionsRemaining.privacyFirstRecommendation: Preserve the community when other members remain, but DETACH/ANONYMIZE creator provenance. Delete the community only when a separate lifecycle rule says the community itself should end.

authorityDecisionsRemaining.why: Event creation requires membership/rules acceptance, while created_by is exposed provenance rather than ongoing authorization.
authorityDecisionsRemaining.privacyFirstRecommendation: Preserve a still-valid multi-party event while de-identifying the erased creator, unless product policy says organizer identity is essential to the event's validity.

authorityDecisionsRemaining.why: Report content may remain bounded moderation evidence after account erasure, but keeping the reporter's canonical user id is a separate necessity question.
authorityDecisionsRemaining.privacyFirstRecommendation: Retain bounded report evidence while ANONYMIZING/DETACHING reporter identity unless an active documented investigation/legal hold specifically requires attribution.

authorityDecisionsRemaining.why: Rules acceptance is minimal evidentiary data (version + accepted_at) tied directly to the user. Its post-erasure necessity cannot be decided from product behavior alone.
authorityDecisionsRemaining.privacyFirstRecommendation: Do not retain identified acceptance evidence after erasure unless privacy/legal review establishes a concrete claims/compliance need and bounded duration.
